WHU Aerial data for external replication¶

This report establishes the data foundation for a future external replication of the RID initialization comparison. It asks whether the official prepared WHU Aerial 0.3 m raster release supplies a clear binary target, reproducible provider roles, and enough spatial information for the same sampling design. No model is trained here, and no WHU test image is used for qualitative analysis or example selection.

The audit distinguishes direct file observations from provider statements. The official dataset page describes Christchurch aerial imagery, the documented tile blocks and the original LINZ source. The associated paper is Ji, Wei and Lu (2019), doi:10.1109/TGRS.2018.2858817.

Data identity and provider roles¶

The downloaded object is the provider's prepared 0.3 m archive with raster labels. It is distinct from the 0.2 m COCO product, both satellite products and the original large aerial mosaic. The provider publishes no trusted checksum for this archive, so the SHA-256 below is a locally computed byte identity rather than an authenticity proof.

The archive is paired strictly by filename within each supplied role. Missing or unexpected files stop preparation; nothing is silently repaired.

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from roofseg.integrity import load_json
from roofseg.whu_data import plot_provider_split_schematic, plot_whu_examples

ROOT = Path.cwd()
manifest = load_json(ROOT / "data/metadata/whu/data_manifest.json")
splits = load_json(ROOT / "data/metadata/whu/splits.json")
audit = load_json(ROOT / "reports/whu_data_audit.json")

identity = pd.DataFrame({
    "field": ["Variant", "Archive bytes", "Local SHA-256", "Pairs", "Provider roles"],
    "observed value": [
        manifest["dataset"]["variant"], manifest["dataset"]["archive_bytes"],
        manifest["dataset"]["archive_sha256"], manifest["audit"]["pair_count"],
        str(splits["counts"]),
    ],
})
identity
field observed value
0 Variant prepared 0.3 m raster images and labels
1 Archive bytes 5432920408
2 Local SHA-256 62a4b4ef0fdfc98deee44b29fd0fe949554a928e1e9d38...
3 Pairs 8188
4 Provider roles {'train': 4736, 'val': 1036, 'test': 2416}

Observed result. The role directories contain 4,736 training, 1,036 validation and 2,416 test pairs, or 8,188 pairs altogether. This agrees with the arithmetic printed on the provider page, although its surrounding prose states 8,189 tiles. The downloadable files and their role arithmetic are the operational contract; the discrepancy is retained in the manifest rather than concealed.

Raster and target contract¶

Every file was opened and checked. Images must be 512 × 512, three-band uint8 TIFFs; labels must be 512 × 512, one-band uint8 TIFFs containing only 0 and 1. Development-pair inspection establishes the direction of this archive's binary code: all-one masks align with tiles containing no buildings, while zero-valued regions align with visible building footprints. The model target is therefore mask == 0.

This target differs conceptually from RID. WHU rasterizes edited building footprints across ordinary map tiles. RID supplies roof-centred samples and codes visible roof segments. A future comparison can replicate an initialization contrast, but it cannot make annotation effort or target semantics identical.

contract = pd.DataFrame({
    "property": ["Image shape", "Mask shape", "Image dtype/range", "Mask values",
                 "Binary target", "CRS", "Physical pixel size in TIFF", "Invalid pixels"],
    "verified value": [
        manifest["audit"]["image_shapes_chw"], manifest["audit"]["mask_shapes_chw"],
        f"{manifest['audit']['image_dtypes']}, {manifest['audit']['image_value_range']}",
        manifest["audit"]["mask_values_observed"], "mask == 0", manifest["audit"]["crs_values"],
        "absent; 0.3 m is provider documentation", not manifest["audit"]["all_pixels_valid_by_file_mask"],
    ],
})
contract
property verified value
0 Image shape [[3, 512, 512]]
1 Mask shape [[1, 512, 512]]
2 Image dtype/range ['uint8'], [0, 255]
3 Mask values [0, 1]
4 Binary target mask == 0
5 CRS [None]
6 Physical pixel size in TIFF absent; 0.3 m is provider documentation
7 Invalid pixels False

The prepared TIFFs have no CRS, non-identity physical transform, ground-control points or nodata declaration. Their identity transform is a pixel-index convention, not a one-metre georeference. All dataset-mask pixels are valid, so future loss and metrics need no WHU-specific validity mask unless later preprocessing introduces padding.

Development examples¶

The following examples are selected deterministically from training and validation metadata by building-area criteria: a typical non-empty training tile, a sparse validation target near its positive 10th percentile, the densest validation target, and an empty target. This exposes both ordinary and difficult class-balance cases without looking at test imagery. Red overlays denote the binary building target.

figure = plot_whu_examples(manifest, ROOT)
figure_path = ROOT / "reports/figures/06_whu_development_examples.png"
figure_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
figure.savefig(figure_path, dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

Interpretation. The examples show that the mask geometry follows building footprints rather than RID's roof-segment taxonomy. Empty and very sparse tiles are legitimate background cases, not missing labels. They must remain in training and evaluation, with the empty-target metric convention stated before any pilot.

Completeness, class balance and exact duplicates¶

The audit reports mask area by provider role and hashes each image and label. Repeated empty masks are expected byte duplicates and do not imply repeated scenery; exact image duplicates and exact image–mask pair duplicates are stronger leakage signals. Only aggregate test-role statistics are used for this technical audit, never test imagery or per-tile examples.

role_summary = pd.DataFrame(audit["role_summaries"]).T
role_summary.index.name = "provider role"
role_summary.style.format({
    "minimum": "{:.3%}", "median": "{:.3%}",
    "mean": "{:.3%}", "maximum": "{:.3%}",
})

The pairing audit found no missing role member because preparation would fail before writing these records. There is one repeated-mask group containing all 1,403 empty masks and no other mask; identical all-background rasters are expected and do not imply repeated scenery. No image or complete image–mask pair is byte-identical, either within or across roles. Hash equality cannot detect shifted, resampled or otherwise near-duplicate views.

What can be verified about geographic separation?¶

The provider documents one 64 × 74 training block, one 14 × 74 evaluation block, and two test blocks of 17 × 42 and 23 × 74 tiles. Its map depicts separate source areas. The schematic below preserves only those stated dimensions; it deliberately does not invent relative coordinates from filenames.

figure = plot_provider_split_schematic()
split_path = ROOT / "reports/figures/06_whu_provider_split_schematic.png"
figure.savefig(split_path, dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

spatial_checks = pd.Series({
    "Embedded georeferencing": splits["spatial_audit"]["embedded_georeferencing"],
    "Per-tile coordinates": splits["spatial_audit"]["per_tile_coordinates_available"],
    "Numeric order treated as coordinates": splits["spatial_audit"]["numeric_order_used_as_coordinates"],
    "Cross-role exact image duplicates": splits["spatial_audit"]["exact_cross_role_image_duplicates"],
    "Cross-role exact pair duplicates": splits["spatial_audit"]["exact_cross_role_pair_duplicates"],
}, name="verified value").to_frame()
spatial_checks
verified value
Embedded georeferencing False
Per-tile coordinates False
Numeric order treated as coordinates False
Cross-role exact image duplicates 0
Cross-role exact pair duplicates 0

Verified finding and limitation. The provider roles are distinct file sets, and exact cross-role image/pair hashes are checked. However, the prepared release does not expose physical tile footprints. The documented region layout supports retaining the provider split, but complete visible-area overlap cannot be recomputed independently. The statement that crop order can recover the mosaic is insufficient to assume a particular row/column convention or global placement without an explicit index map.

This also prevents a defensible spatial-maximin sample selection. Numeric names remain identifiers only.

Proposed bounded pilot¶

The split record predeclares one label-independent, uniform sample of 100 IDs from the provider training role using an isolated NumPy generator with seed 17. Validation remains the provider validation region, and the provider test role remains outside subset selection, checkpoint choice and qualitative analysis.

pilot = splits["future_pilot_subset"]
pilot_checks = pd.Series({
    "Stored IDs": len(pilot["ids"]),
    "Unique IDs": len(set(pilot["ids"])),
    "All belong to training": set(pilot["ids"]) <= set(splits["roles"]["train"]),
    "Overlap with validation": len(set(pilot["ids"]) & set(splits["roles"]["val"])),
    "Overlap with test": len(set(pilot["ids"]) & set(splits["roles"]["test"])),
    "Subset seed": pilot["seed"],
}, name="value").to_frame()
pilot_checks
value
Stored IDs 100
Unique IDs 100
All belong to training True
Overlap with validation 0
Overlap with test 0
Subset seed 17

The proposed next block is exactly two fresh n=100 runs: Random initialization versus the original ImageNet EfficientNet-B0 encoder, both with a newly initialized decoder and the existing common 4,000-update rule (1e-3 through update 2,000, then 1e-4). IDs, order seed, augmentation seed and validation must be paired. Before training, the loader and normalization must be adapted explicitly to WHU's RGB TIFF and inverted 0/1 target contract, while the loss and metrics can use all pixels.

This pilot would test whether the direction of the pretraining advantage recurs in a different city and footprint-label product. It would not prove geographic generalization within WHU, equal annotation effort to RID, or robustness to training-image selection. A second stored uniform subset should be considered only after the first paired result is reviewed.

Conclusion¶

The prepared WHU data are technically suitable for a bounded external-replication pilot: pairing, binary labels, role membership and byte identity are reproducible. The principal unresolved limitation is spatial metadata. Provider roles should be retained, the test role should stay locked, and spatial-maximin selection should not be claimed from this release. No training or RID test evaluation was performed in this stage.
